parts.title: SPIRAL REVIEW (5 min)
content: 1. GRAMMAR SPIRAL: Rewrite these sentences as PASSIVE VOICE with citation: a) 'Scientists discovered that dolphins dream.' → 'It was discovered by scientists that...' b) 'WWF reported that tigers are endangered.'
2. VOCABULARY: Arrange in order of how to use evidence in a paragraph: [a] write your comment, [b] introduce the quote/paraphrase, [c] add the citation, [d] present the evidence
3. MATH SPIRAL: Your research data shows: 65% of experts think plastic bans are effective, 25% are unsure, 10% disagree. Draw a bar chart to represent this data. Label the X and Y axes correctly.

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  Academic writing uses evidence to support ideas. There are two main ways to include evidence from sources: DIRECT QUOTES and PARAPHRASES.
content: 📖 Academic writing uses evidence to support ideas. There are two main ways to include evidence from sources: DIRECT QUOTES and PARAPHRASES.

A DIRECT QUOTE uses the exact words from the source, placed in quotation marks (' '). Use direct quotes when the original wording is powerful or precise. Always introduce the quote with a signal phrase: According to Dr. Smith, 'exact words here.'
A PARAPHRASE uses your own words to restate the source's idea. Paraphrases are more common in academic writing because they show you truly understand the information.

A CITATION tells the reader where the information came from. In your Passion Project report, a simple citation format is: (Author, Year). For example: Dolphins are highly intelligent mammals (WWF, 2022).
Every fact in your report that came from a source needs a citation. At the end of your report, you will list all sources in a BIBLIOGRAPHY.
